They run a single-page web widget that calls Redwood hosted_api directly from their backend. Key snippets from discovery call and SE troubleshooting below.

Use-case details / requirements:
- Primary: real-time chat (support-agent) for web & mobile widget, average session length 4 messages, average prompt length ~120-300 tokens incl. system + history.
- Secondary: on-demand summarization of long tickets (~2-4k tokens) used asynchronously.
- Latency targets: p95 < 800ms for streaming chat, p99 ideally < 2s. Cost sensitivity: high — small ARR, want predictable unit costs.
- Model preference: open / community models acceptable; prefer smallest model that meets quality SLO.

Technical notes / SE recommendations given:
- Region choice: recommend deploy traffic to nearest Redwood region (us-west-2 for west coast + EU edge to be investigated). For EU users suggest trying eu-west-1 region to measure hop reduction; current DNS/routing resolved to us-east which increased RTT.
- Timeout settings: front-end timeout at 10s is too aggressive for request-level timeouts; recommend 60s client timeout for streaming and 30s for non-streaming generation with exponential backoff on retries.
- Prompt length guidance: trim system prompts and only include last 6 user turns; set max_tokens to 512 for chat to cap tail latency; use token counting on client to drop old history.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: streaming enabled for UX; ensure chunking threshold set low so first byte returns fast.
- Caching & prefix reuse: enable prefix (KV) caching for repeated system messages and static context (e.g., company policy text). This reduced tokens in internal POC by ~18%.
- Batching: not applicable for interactive chat, but recommended for embeddings and bulk summarization jobs during off-peak windows.

Customer quotes: "We see a handful of sessions where the UI hangs and users abandon chat — want predictable p99s"; "Cost is a big factor, can't justify overprovisioned dedicated capacity yet".
